correctness.rationale: Edge independence makes commutation exactly the determinant-zero constraints on each graph edge; the induced-support connected components and outside-neighborhood free coordinates give the centralizer dimension. Connected domination is equivalent to projective isolation. The join across complementary components forces mixed-block isolation and forbids cross-block commuting edges. Every nonisolated block point reaches a commuting basis line within two steps; basis lines form the connected complement component. Weighted support enumeration and the tree internal-vertex characterization give the exact counts. The direct bracket verifier checked full component partitions in 2950 labeled graph/field cases over F2 and F3. Finite tests are not used as proof of generality.

originality.rationale: Primary texts were examined for the same quotient/projective vertex set and for results that imply the component census. Sriwongsa studies the opposite adjacency relation on exactly the projective quotient; its Theorem 2.12 already implies the general isolated-vertex criterion for the complementary commuting graph, and no novelty is claimed for that. Its noncommuting-graph connectivity does not imply classification of positive-size connected components of the complement. Ha et al. give general methods for elementwise commuting graphs but not a co-component classification with connected-domination counts for edge-distinct graph Lie algebras. The source graph Lie construction (Godoy Molina and Lagos) does not state the nontrivial-component result. Existing support rank identities imply only the isolation criterion; the classification of all nontrivial projective connected components requires distinct cross-block and two-step-connectivity arguments. Finite-field direct checks agree. Equivalence under different terminology is an admitted residual risk.
residual_risks: A statement equivalent to the projective commuting co-component theorem might be indexed in a different graph-Lie or commuting-geometry vocabulary.

The isolation criterion is a specialization of Sriwongsa Theorem 2.12 (projective noncommuting domination) and follows from support-centralizer ranks, so it is explicitly not claimed as independently new; the main contribution is the full nontrivial connected-component classification and explicit graph-specific enumeration.
Small-prime-field experiments do not validate infinite quantifiers; the all-prime-power proof uses elementary coordinate algebra.

value.rationale: An all-graph classification of projective commuting components is a natural structural invariant for graph-indexed class-two Lie algebras, not a renamed single-rank statistic. The exact connected-domination polynomial translates algebraic commutation geometry into graph structure; the tree leaf formula gives an explicit recoverable natural graph invariant and a structural star/nonstar boundary. Arbitrary simple graphs and finite prime-power fields are covered. The scope does not overclaim tree isomorphism reconstruction or exact component spectra.
